To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypermedia and virtual environments are complementary and that the combination of hypermedia and 3D virtual environments can be a very powerful tool for supporting remote collaboration.

1) the design of a virtual project room for collaborative work requires the integration of 3D design models with other kinds of documents, 2) the integration of hyperdocuments with virtual environments can be achieved in a number of ways, and 3) the design of the user interface for the virtual project room requires careful design of the user's spatial perception of the environment.
(1) the notion of hypermedia is not limited to 2D documents and (2) the notion of virtual project room is a useful concept for designing CSCW tools for (landscape) architects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of open hypermedia technology with virtual environments, and the design of open hypermedia services for virtual environments.
the integration of open hypermedia with virtual environments, in particular collaborative virtual environments.
how to support collaboration in the virtual environment by means of open hypermedia technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the integration of 3D spatial environments and hypermedia is a complex issue, which requires careful design and implementation.
we are still at the beginning of the design of hypermedia in the virtual environment.
hypermedia and collaborative work are not yet integrated into the design of virtual project rooms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of hypermediated documents in the 3D virtual project room is a promising approach to support remote collaboration between landscape architects and architects.
the notion of a virtual project room, based on open hypermedia technology, is an appropriate means for supporting collaborative work in the design domain.

hypermedia and collaborative technologies should be integrated to provide a notion of virtual spaces that support a variety of collaboration and information access patterns, including the ability to move between the different spaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of hyperlinks and spatiality in the virtual project rooms is not a straightforward task.

the design of a collaborative virtual environment for a specific domain is not only a matter of providing a virtual environment, it is also a matter of designing the hypermedia aspects of this environment.

the notion of a virtual project room should be open, and should support the integration of arbitrary media, including 3D design models and documents, in order to provide the flexibility needed for collaboration.
